newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's drought crisis team to meet May 13.
newsitem.headline: France's drought crisis team to meet May 13.

text.p: A crisis team set up by the French farm ministry to monitor crop and water tables conditions following nearly four months of drought will meet on May 13, a ministry official said on Monday.
The team made up from farm organisations and ministry officials will review crop development and the impact of recent rainfall, the official said.
An official for the FNSEA farmers' union also said the team may discuss a fodder shortage affecting cattle breeders and compensation payments for farmers hit by drought and frost.
The FNSEA said earlier that recent rainfall helped revive grain crops but came too late to limit yield losses already estimated at some 20 percent for winter soft wheat and barley.
It also put yield losses at between 40 and 70 percent for fodder.

Weather experts say rain since the last week of April has improved crop conditions but underground water tables are still 50 percent below normal. Last week seven new French departments took water restriction measures, bringing to 25 the number of departments hit by the curbs since early April.
